source.dataset: Enron Email Dataset (CALO project; ~517k real corporate e-mails, 150 custodian mailboxes)
source.why_this_source: The CMU distribution is the reputable primary source: it is the official, currently reachable archive (HTTP 200, byte ranges supported) maintained by CMU, it is the May 7 2015 version with the FERC privacy deletions applied (per CMU DELETIONS.txt), and it is plain-text mail that can be streamed with the standard library alone. The HuggingFace mirror corbt/enron-emails (517,401 rows, parquet; columns message_id, subject, from, to, cc, bcc, date, body, file_name) was evaluated and rejected as the primary source: its dataset card README is empty, so it declares no license and no provenance chain back to a specific CMU release, and it needs the optional pyarrow package. The parquet reader is still implemented as a documented alternative.
source.license_and_terms: The Enron corpus was released into the public record by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) during its investigation of Enron Corporation; it is public as government records and is widely used for non-commercial research. CMU distributes it 'as a resource for researchers who are interested in improving current email tools, or understanding how email is currently used' and explicitly asks users to 'be sensitive to the privacy of the people involved' (https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~enron/). Citation: Klimt & Yang, 'The Enron Corpus: A New Dataset for Email Classification Research' (paper linked by the CMU page, http://ceas.cc/2004/168.pdf, presented at the 2004 CEAS conference). The dataset ships without attachments and with employee-requested deletions applied.
source.redaction_and_anonymity: Every mined row is redacted before writing with consistent placeholder tokens: names -> [NAME], e-mail addresses -> [EMAIL], company names -> [COMPANY] (Enron itself and <Name> + corporate-suffix patterns), phone numbers and long digit runs -> [PHONE], SSN/card-shaped numbers -> [ID], street addresses, floor/suite lines and city-state-zip blocks -> [ADDRESS], URLs -> [URL]. Name tokens are harvested per run from message addresses and capitalised name pairs and replaced wherever they appear capitalised; greeting/signature/title names are forced to [NAME]. Redaction runs in a loop until no PII class changes. Evidence quotes are extracted AFTER redaction, so no raw personal data can appear in any row field. A per-row programmatic sweep of EVERY PII class (e-mail addresses, phone-shaped numbers, long digit runs, SSN/card shapes, street addresses, floor/suite lines, city-state-zip blocks, URLs, company references, capitalised name-lexicon words) must report zero leftovers; ANY row with a leftover is DROPPED entirely, so redaction is absolute. Source mailbox paths and message headers are never written to the outputs. With these substitutions the rows are non-identifying: they contain no names, e-mail addresses, company names, phone numbers, addresses, ID numbers or URLs from the original messages.

rejection_share.note: Fail-closed mining over all scanned corpus messages found only 0 messages carrying a clear negative hiring decision about the recipient's own application (0 unique after redaction+dedup) and ALL of them are included in the output. The 25-35% share is not reachable from real data without relabelling soft, conditional or ambiguous mail as rejection, which the fail-closed policy (task requirement: label rejection ONLY on a clear negative decision) forbids. The rejection share is therefore reported as-is rather than inflated.

orchestrator_reverification.evidence_substring_invariant: 100% on all 2168 rows (checked against parsed untrusted_email field)
